To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rendezvous can always be completed in O (n log l) steps in graphs, and this complexity cannot be improved for certain graphs.

rendezvous in graphs with simultaneous startup can be completed at a cost of O(n + log(l)) on any n-node network, and with arbitrary startup, at a cost of Θ(n2) on some n-node networks, but at a cost of only O(n2 log l + nτ) on any n- node network.

(1) rendezvous on trees with simultaneous startup is optimal, (2) rendezvous on rings with simultaneous startup is sub-optimal, (3) rendezvous on graphs with arbitrary startup is sub-opti- mal, (4) rendezvous on all connected graphs with arbitrary startup can be done in polynomial time, and (5) rendezvous on some graphs with simultaneous startup cannot be done in polynomial cost

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, with simultaneous or arbitrary startup, rendezvous in any connected graph can be achieved at cost O(n2 log l).
, for any connected graph, there exists an efficient rendezvous algorithm if the agents are allowed to start their execution simultaneously.

, in the deterministic setting, rendezvous can be achieved at cost O(n2) in the worst case, and O(n log l) in the best case, where l is smaller of the two agents' identifiers, and n is the number of nodes in the graph.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rendezvous is fast in graphs with bounded degree, but it can be very slow on general graphs.

rendezvous in graphs with arbitrary startup is hard to achieve and the complexity of rendezvous in graphs is not known, whereas rendezvous in trees is easy, but the complexity of rendezvousing on trees is still an open question.
, in general graphs, rendezvous with simultaneous startup is possible at cost O(n2), while with arbitrary startup, rendezvous is possible at cost polynomial in n and τ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for deterministic rendezvous in graphs, the initial distance between the agents plays a crucial role.
, for the rendezvous problem, the class of graphs with bounded degree is a natural class, where the rendezvous problem can be solved optimally.
rendezvous can always be achieved with polynomial cost.
